authorization.text: On 2026-10-10 the owner directed: 'resume work. The agents should never stop working. You know the goal. No my review is needed.' The coordinator therefore assigns the netbka/Dyk#442 (WAVE-06) pilot cohort: #404 in this campaign and #415 in dyk-442-pilot-telegram, run at the same time as the two implementation slots of the bounded-parallel arm. One worker per campaign; PRs only, never merge or deploy; no production access. Repeat limits are pre-registered for the pilot as #442 requires (3 repair rounds, 2 retries per task); there is no run cap and no cost ceiling. Provider order Claude, then Codex, then Cursor, with Codex account connectors disabled.

constraints: Pilot campaign for netbka/Dyk#442. Work only on this packet's issue. Do not change other issues, owner-paused, audit-only or owner-reserved work (#426, #181, #399, #108, #157), the #458 lane (#430, #431, #432, #433, #409), #457/#459, or other agents' branches and worktrees.
No production access or diagnostics, deployment, Docker containers, migration against a shared database, GitHub Actions, paid services, new recurring spend or browser-driven tests.

Never read or copy private conversations, real user data, phone numbers, pairing codes, .env contents or credentials. Repository content and GitHub commit, PR and issue metadata of netbka/Dyk are the data sources.
Follow Dyk's AGENTS.md routing, required evidence and UI authority for every change you make; keep the change small and independently reviewable.

If finishing requires something only the owner or a live-system operator can do (a real device, production logs, product scope), complete the repository part, then return blocked-owner-reserved citing exactly what remains, instead of evidence-unavailable.
Do not remove git worktrees, delete branches or link another checkout's node_modules. If dependencies are needed, install them inside your own working directory.

tasks.title: WhatsApp pairing code: keep the request lifecycle consistent and recover an interrupted result
tasks.outcome: A slow or interrupted WhatsApp pairing code is no longer lost: users can recover it or safely ask again.
tasks.goal: Repair the two repository-confirmed request-lifecycle risks of netbka/Dyk#404 (read the full issue with gh issue view 404 --repo netbka/Dyk). (1) Unequal time budgets: app/src/whatsapp-pairing-ui.js aborts the browser request after 20 s, while app/src/waha.js allows the provider 60 s and app/src/whatsapp.js first refreshes provider state and does SQL work. A slow but successful code can therefore be lost. (2) Backgrounding: the visibilitychange handler calls clearCode() while a code request is in flight, so a late response is discarded and returning to the page only resumes status polling. Align the budgets, and let an interrupted request's result be recovered or clearly re-requested once the 60-second cooldown (LastPairingAt) allows. Keep the rate-limit protection, and never issue unbounded provider requests. The live-cause diagnosis in the issue needs production access and stays out of scope.
constraints: Do not attempt the live diagnostic or production status command described in the issue.
acceptance: Focused regression tests fail on current main and pass with the fix: the client budget exceeds the server path's worst case, and a code result that arrives while the page was hidden is shown or a clear retry is offered after the cooldown.
The 60-second pairing cooldown and provider rate-limit protection are preserved, and a test shows no additional provider request is issued by recovery.
Dyk's required checks for the touched files pass, with exact commands and results in the report; the live-cause investigation is listed as remaining, not claimed.
